filename: Deep Learning for Subgrid‐Scale Turbulence Modeling in Large‐Eddy Simulations of the Convective Atmospheric Boundary Layer.pdf
title: Deep Learning for Subgrid-Scale Turbulence Modeling in Large-Eddy Simulations of the Convective Atmospheric Boundary Layer
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
ml_methods: Dense Neural Networks with 3D local stencils
host_model: Kumar et al. (2006) mixed pseudospectral/finite-difference LES code
testbed_rationale: High-resolution DNS and filtered 3D boundary layer turbulence datasets under multiple stability regimes are publicly deposited with a permanent DOI on Columbia Academic Commons, making it directly suited for subgrid-scale ML parameterization development.
pain_points: Simultaneously capturing both SGS stress correlation and SGS energy dissipation in online simulations without numerical instability or energy pileup
Aliasing errors when computing SGS stresses from discrete simulation grids
Generalization across distinct stability regimes (from shear-dominated to highly convective boundary layers)
Treatment of near-wall surface flux conditions and sponge layers when replacing algebraic closures with ML models
extraction_notes: The code for the LES solver and DNN coupling was not stated in a dedicated code availability statement, but the data is shared via Columbia Academic Commons DOI.
